create.name: Daifukuji Soto Mission
create.bio:
Daifukuji Soto Mission is a Japanese Soto Zen temple in Honalo, in the Kona district on the west side of Hawaiʻi Island, whose name means Temple of Great Happiness. Its story begins in 1914, when the Reverend Kaiseki Kodama arrived to serve the Japanese families farming coffee in the area; the present main hall, a mix of Western and Japanese building styles, was dedicated in 1921 and is now on the National Register of Historic Places. The Reverend Jiko Nakade, who grew up in Kona and trained through the Hawaiʻi Soto Shu ministers' programme, is its twelfth resident minister and the first woman to hold that post.

Today the membership is mixed in age and background. Zazen is offered on weekday mornings and a Monday evening, with beginners' instruction by appointment and a temple meditation group for those who want to commit further. Sunday family services, a monthly Kannon service with chanting and music, a Dharma study group, sutra-copying and buddha-tracing as quiet meditation, and a Sunday programme for young children sit alongside cultural groups such as taiko and Bon dance. The temple's YouTube channel carries services, talks and a short beginners' series on sitting at home.

courses.title: Zen Meditation (Zazen) at Daifukuji
courses.description: Sitting meditation in the temple on Wednesday and Friday mornings and on Monday evenings, with a short morning service on Wednesdays and occasional evening study. Newcomers can book a first lesson in sitting, walking meditation and hall etiquette.

courses.title: Sunday Family Services and Kannon Services
courses.description: Family services for all ages are held on two or three Sunday mornings a month, with a minute of sitting, songs, chanting and a short talk. On the third Wednesday morning of each month a Kannon service brings candlelight, chanting and traditional music.

courses.title: Temple Groups and Study
courses.description: Regular temple groups including a Dharma study group open to all, silent sutra copying and buddha tracing as art meditation, a women's spirituality circle and a Dharma programme for young children. Some groups are for temple members only.

free_resources.title: Try Sit Meditation Series
free_resources.description: Ten short videos in which Rev. Jiko Nakade walks beginners through starting a home sitting practice: posture on a chair or floor, hands, eyes, breath and the wandering mind. Free on the temple's YouTube channel.

flags: Base: the temple stands in Honalo (a small Kona community); the contact page's mailing address is Kealakekua, used as the city. Owner may prefer Honalo or Kona.

Photos: the temple-front image is a wide banner (800x200) from the site's allowed /background_new/ folder; the larger photos are in /picture/, which robots.txt disallows, so not used. Second image is the channel avatar, a line-drawing logo.
No hub links: resident minister Rev. Jiko Nakade is not on Spiritpedia; teachers file written with an empty list. Possible future listing: Jiko Nakade.
Ten of the eleven videos are the short Try Sit beginners' series (6–11 minutes each) and the same series is the free resource (playlist).
Temple also hosts cultural and social groups (taiko, Bon dance, orchid club, walking group, qigong); not listed as items.
left_out: Mochi and takuan pickle cooking videos (most-viewed after Try Sit #5): cultural cooking, not teaching.
Visions of Kannon (2021) and other short chants and songs: content not checked or under ~4 minutes.
Weddings, blessings and memorial services: rites by arrangement, not offerings.
Qigong sessions, walking group, taiko, Bon dance, Japanese classes: community activities rather than the temple's own Zen programme.
Zazenkai membership (form on zazen.html): same page as the zazen offering.
